Customising Markers

Source: vignettes/articles/markers.Rmd
markers.Rmd

This article covers the many ways magicIcons() markers can be customised. It uses the same port_talbot data and scales as Getting Started:

library(leaflet)
library(leaf.magic)

port_talbot$open_year <- as.integer(format(port_talbot$start_date, "%Y"))
port_talbot$popup <- paste0(
  "<strong>", toupper(port_talbot$site), "</strong> (", port_talbot$code, ")",
  "<hr>Site Type: ", port_talbot$site_type,
  "<br>Opened: ", port_talbot$open_year
)

site_types <- c("Urban Industrial", "Urban Background", "Urban Traffic")
iconPal <- iconFactor(c("house", "industry", "car"), domain = site_types)
catPal <- colorFactor(c("#12436D", "#28A197", "#801650"), domain = site_types)

Icons

Icon Libraries

By default, magicIcons() uses Font Awesome icons, but the library argument lets you choose from four icon libraries. Each is provided by a different package, which you’ll need to have installed to use it:

library Icons Package
"fontawesome" https://fontawesome.com/search?ic=free fontawesome
"bootstrap" https://icons.getbootstrap.com/ bsicons
"lucide" https://lucide.dev/icons/ lucidr
"ionicons" https://ionic.io/ionicons None - icons are downloaded when first used, so require an internet connection

For example, here are some Lucide icons:

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = "factory",
      library = "lucide"
    )
  )

Text Markers

Sometimes the best “icon” is a short piece of text, like a number or a letter. Setting library = "text" shows icon as text inside the marker. Text shrinks to fit as it gets longer, so it works best with up to around three characters.

For example, we can label each site with the last two digits of the year it opened:

yearPal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = port_talbot$open_year)

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ format(start_date, "%y"),
      markerColor = ~ yearPal(open_year),
      marker = "circle",
      library = "text"
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    pal = yearPal,
    values = ~open_year,
    title = "Opening Year",
    labFormat = labelFormat(big.mark = "")
  )

Custom SVG Icons

If the icon you need isn’t in any of the icon libraries, library = "svg" lets you provide your own icon as a string of SVG markup. Any parts of the SVG which have no fill of their own (or use currentColor) take on iconColor, while any hard-coded colours are kept.

bolt <- '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M13 2 4 14h7l-1 8 9-12h-7z"/></svg>'

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = bolt,
      markerColor = "#28A197",
      library = "svg"
    )
  )

Colours

magicIcons() has two arguments related to colour; markerColor which colours the marker, and iconColor which colours the icon. Any colour can be supplied to these arguments - either a constant value or colour values mapped to a column using, for example, leaflet::colorFactor(). iconColor defaults to "auto", which picks black or white for each marker, whichever contrasts more with its markerColor.

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
      markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),
      iconColor = "#F7F7F7"
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    pal = catPal,
    values = ~site_type,
    title = "Site Type"
  )

leaf.magic also exports the awesomePalette list, which are hex codes for the colours used in leaflet::awesomeIcons(). You could use these if you want to recreate the colour scheme of awesomeIcons() with the flexibility of magicIcons().

cols <- names(awesomePalette)[names(awesomePalette) != "white"]
breweries91$facolor <- sample(cols, nrow(breweries91), replace = TRUE)
breweries91$hexcolor <- unlist(awesomePalette[breweries91$facolor], use.names = FALSE)

leaflet(breweries91) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addAwesomeMarkers(
    icon = ~ awesomeIcons(
      icon = "circle",
      markerColor = facolor,
      iconColor = "#FFFFFF",
      library = "fa"
    ),
    group = "Awesome"
  ) |>
  addMarkers(
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = "circle",
      markerColor = ~hexcolor,
      iconColor = "#FFFFFF"
    ),
    group = "Magic"
  ) |>
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("Awesome", "Magic")
  )

Size

Unlike leaflet::awesomeIcons(), magicIcons() can be easily re-sized. Much like in leaflet::addCircleMarkers(), this can vary with another variable; let’s make the closed sites a bit smaller than the open ones with markerSize, which sets the width of the marker in pixels. Note the default is 30L, which is roughly the same size as the default leaflet::addMarkers() marker.

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
      markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),
      markerSize = ~ ifelse(open, 30L, 20L)
    )
  )

Shapes

While the default marker type, the “tear-drop” marker, is useful in most instances, you may find other marker shapes of interest. These are:

  • Pointed shapes, which sit on their location with their tip, like the default marker: "marker", "marker-square" (a pin with a square head) and "callout" (a speech bubble).

  • Centred shapes, which sit centred on their location: "circle", "square", "diamond", "triangle", "hexagon", "star" and "heart".

  • "none", which removes the marker entirely and places the icon directly on the map itself. With no marker to contrast with, an "auto" iconColor takes on the markerColor instead.

Use the layer control in the map below to try them out.

shapes <- c(
  "marker", "marker-square", "callout", "circle", "square", "diamond",
  "triangle", "hexagon", "star", "heart", "none"
)

map <- leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles()

for (shape in shapes) {
  map <- map |>
    addMarkers(
      popup = ~popup,
      icon = magicIcons(
        icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
        markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),
        marker = shape
      ),
      group = shape
    )
}

map |>
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = shapes,
    options = layersControlOptions(FALSE)
  ) |>
  addIconLegend(
    position = "bottomleft",
    pal = iconPal,
    values = ~site_type,
    colors = catPal,
    title = "Site Type"
  )

Note that marker can vary with some variable, allowing the marker shape itself to encode extra information. As marker shapes are just names, iconFactor() can map data to them.

markPal <- iconFactor(c("circle", "diamond", "square"), site_types)

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(icon = magicIcons(
    marker = ~ markPal(site_type),
    markerSize = ~ ifelse(markPal(site_type) == "diamond", 35, 30)
  )) |>
  addIconLegend(
    pal = markPal,
    values = ~site_type,
    title = "Site Type"
  )

Custom Shapes

If none of the built-in shapes suit, you can design your own with markerShape(). A shape is drawn with SVG in its own coordinate system - by default, 100 units wide and 100 units tall - and you tell markerShape():

  • path: the outline of the shape, as SVG path data or SVG markup.
  • icon: the centre (x, y) and size of the square the icon is drawn in.
  • anchor: the point of the shape that sits on the marker’s location.
  • popup: where popups open from.

The shape is filled with markerColor and given a darker outline for you. For example, here’s a downward-pointing arrow, anchored at its tip:

arrow <- markerShape(
  path = "M2 2h96L50 98z",
  icon = c(x = 50, y = 34, size = 36),
  anchor = c(x = 50, y = 98),
  popup = c(x = 50, y = 10),
  shadow = "cast"
)

arrow
#> <markerShape> 100 x 100
#> * icon: size 36 centred at (50, 34)
#> * anchor: (50, 98)
#> * popup: (50, 10)
#> * shadow: cast

A custom shape can be passed to marker just like a built-in one. To use a different shape for each marker, give marker a list of shapes and/or shape names. Here, open sites use the arrow and closed sites use a circle.

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
      markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),
      marker = ~ lapply(open, \(x) if (x) arrow else "circle")
    )
  ) |>
  addIconLegend(
    pal = iconPal,
    values = ~site_type,
    colors = catPal,
    title = "Site Type"
  )

Shadows

Like the default leaflet marker, leaf.magic markers have shadows. Pointed shapes cast a shadow up and to the right from their tip, as if they were standing on the map, while other shapes have a soft shadow just beneath them. Shadows are drawn underneath all of the markers, so a marker’s shadow never covers another marker.

Shadows can be turned off with shadow = FALSE. Use the layer control below to compare. For custom shapes, the shadow argument of markerShape() chooses between a "cast" shadow, a "drop" shadow, or "none".

addShadowMarkers <- function(map, shadow) {
  map |>
    addMarkers(
      popup = ~popup,
      icon = magicIcons(
        icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
        markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),
        shadow = shadow
      ),
      group = if (shadow) "With Shadows" else "Without Shadows"
    )
}

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addShadowMarkers(TRUE) |>
  addShadowMarkers(FALSE) |>
  addLayersControl(
    baseGroups = c("With Shadows", "Without Shadows"),
    options = layersControlOptions(FALSE)
  )

Outlines

Each marker has a thin outline in a slightly darker shade of its colour. outlineColor and outlineWidth (in pixels) change this, which can help markers stand out against a busy basemap.

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
      markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type),
      marker = "circle",
      outlineColor = "white",
      outlineWidth = 2
    )
  )

Accessibility

Markers are images, so screen readers can’t tell what they show. leaflet’s markerOptions() can give each marker alternative text with alt, and a tooltip shown when hovering with title. Both can be mapped to your data with a formula, just like popup.

leaflet(port_talbot) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    popup = ~popup,
    icon = magicIcons(
      icon = ~ iconPal(site_type),
      markerColor = ~ catPal(site_type)
    ),
    options = markerOptions(
      alt = ~ paste(site, "-", site_type),
      title = ~site
    )
  )

Caching

Markers are saved to a temporary directory by default, which is cleared at the end of each R session. Each marker is only built once per session, so maps with many repeated markers are quick to draw. If you build the same markers often (for example, in a Shiny app), the dir argument of magicIcons() can point to a permanent directory so that markers are only ever built once.
